problem: Instance navigation under ambiguous user queries (e.g. 'Find the cabinet') is handled by independent matching (AIUTA), which scores each candidate against dialogue facts and commits prematurely to a distractor sharing attributes with the target. Asking open-ended questions about the target also yields long user responses and non-discriminative facts.
motivation: Real user requests are underspecified, so an agent should shoulder the disambiguation burden with minimal user effort. The cue separating a target from similar distractors is inherently comparative, so it should be found by contrasting candidates rather than by describing the target in isolation.
key_idea: First build a candidate pool of same-category instances, then repeatedly extract an attribute-value pair that splits the pool, ask the user a yes/no question about it, and prune all inconsistent candidates at once (Recursive Comparative Judgment).
insight: Deferring the decision until a pool exists gives a large gain (Pooled Independent Matching SR 17.5 vs AIUTA* 10.5 on Val Seen), and comparison over the same pool adds more (23.7 SR) while cutting response length from 460 to 4.2 tokens. This works because each round needs only a splitting attribute, not one that uniquely identifies the target. Ablations on Val Seen show that removing NLI scoring (20.6), similarity-based core set selection (20.5) or refinement (21.8) each hurts SR. A larger pool threshold raises SR but lowers SPL.
method: Pool Construction Stage: a VLFM-based explorer collects category-c detections, and instances are assigned by 3D point-cloud overlap (radius 0.03 m, overlap ≥0.3). Each candidate keeps K=6 DINOv2/K-means representative views arranged as a collage, and an MLLM writes one multi-view description. The stage ends when the pool reaches N_min=5, or at step 400 on CoIN / 600 on TextNav.

Similarity-based core set selection: pairwise similarity is the mean of text-embedding and image-embedding cosine similarity. Greedy peeling (Charikar-style) picks the core set G_c with maximal mean intra-set similarity, and the rest form G_r.

DA discovery: an LLM extracts shared attributes from G_c descriptions, and a DeBERTa-v3-large NLI verifier scores each attribute on every candidate (sigmoid of entail logit minus max of neutral/contradict logits). The attribute maximizing mean score in G_c minus mean score in G_r is chosen.
Property-guided refinement: candidates in G_r whose entailment score for the chosen attribute is ≥ τ=0.9 are moved into G_c.

Interactive pruning: the agent asks a binary yes/no question about the attribute. It keeps G_c on Yes and G_r on No, repeating until one candidate remains. If the answer is No and G_r is empty, the agent resumes pool construction to add a candidate and pre-prunes it with the facts gathered so far.
Exploration heuristics: EMA-based loop detection blacklists frontiers, and a 360° rotation is triggered in open areas to compensate for the 30° FOV.

TextNav adaptation: user questions are disabled, and the attribute set is parsed once from the text goal, so U_{t+1}=G_c always. An LLM verifier compares the final candidate's description with the goal.

setting.backbone: Qwen3-VL-8B (frozen, used as both LLM and MLLM) + DeBERTa-v3-large NLI + DINOv2 + VLFM exploration
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D with 30° FOV, plus pose for mapping; category-only input on CoIN, detailed text goal on TextNav
setting.action_space: discrete low-level: move_forward, turn_left, turn_right, stop, plus optional free-form question
setting.privileged: none at test time; the user simulator is an MLLM that sees the target image

results: ProCompNav gets the highest SR on all CoIN-Bench splits with category-only input (23.7/28.1/17.0). It beats AIUTA* (10.5/15.3/8.9), Pooled Independent Matching (17.5/22.0/13.3) and even description-input Context-Nav (13.5/20.3/11.3) and 3D-Mem*. Total response length falls from ~460 to ~4.2 tokens. On TextNav it reaches SR 28.5, above Context-Nav's 26.2, though SPL is lower (6.9 vs UniGoal 11.4).
limitations: Evaluated only in simulation with an MLLM user simulator, with no real robot or human users.
The pool must reach a minimum size (N_min=5), which is inefficient when few same-category instances exist, and it lowers SPL (SPL is low overall, ~6-8).
Absolute SR is still low (17-28%), and the method depends on the quality of the VLFM exploration backbone and its heuristics.
